title: Inviting, accepting, refusing
why: This lesson puts the future and the conditional to work in real social life: inviting someone, accepting warmly, refusing tactfully with an excuse and suggesting another time. It ends the unit with the phrases you need to fix a time and a place.

{"lessons": ["

Making an invitation

You can invite someone with a simple question (Tu viens au cinéma ?), but French has a few friendly formulas that make an invitation sound natural. Notice that most of them work like \"Do you feel like…?\" or \"How about…?\" in English.

With tuWith vousEnglish
Ça te dit de venir ?Ça vous dirait de venir ?Do you feel like coming? / Would you like to come?
Tu as envie de sortir ?Vous avez envie de sortir ?Do you feel like going out?
On pourrait aller à la plage.Nous pourrions aller à la plage.We could go to the beach.
Si on allait au cinéma ?Si nous allions au cinéma ?How about going to the movies?
Tu es libre samedi ?Vous êtes libre samedi ?Are you free on Saturday?

Ça te dit de and avoir envie de are followed by an infinitive, with de (d' before a vowel): Ça te dit d'aller au restaurant ?

Si on allait… ? uses si + imparfait. Take it as a fixed formula for a suggestion: you'll study si + imparfait properly at B1. On pourrait… is the conditional you just learned: softer than On va…

Il fait beau ! Si on allait se promener au parc ?The weather's nice! How about going for a walk in the park?

Careful with Je t'invite: in a café or a restaurant, it means \"It's my treat\", so the person who says it pays. To just suggest going together, say On va boire un verre ?

", "

Saying yes, saying no

Accepting

FrenchEnglishTone
Avec plaisir !With pleasure!warm, always polite
Volontiers !Gladly! I'd love to!warm, a little formal
Bonne idée !Good idea!neutral
Ça marche !Sounds good! Deal!informal
Pourquoi pas ?Why not?a bit lukewarm

Refusing politely

In France, a plain non sounds abrupt. A polite refusal has three steps: thank the person or say you're sorry, give an excuse, and suggest another time.

Désolée, je ne peux pas, je suis prise samedi. Une autre fois, peut-être ?Sorry, I can't, I'm busy on Saturday. Another time, maybe?

Je suis pris (literally \"I'm taken\") is the usual way to say \"I'm busy, I already have plans\". It agrees: je suis prise for a woman, nous sommes pris. J'ai un empêchement means something has come up: it's handy because you don't have to explain.

Merci pour l'invitation, mais malheureusement j'ai un empêchement. C'est dommage !Thanks for the invitation, but unfortunately something has come up. What a shame!

Suggesting another time

Use the conditional of aller (to suit): Et dimanche, ça t'irait ? (Would Sunday work for you?) or, with vous, ça vous irait ? You can also use the future: On ira la semaine prochaine.

Désolé agrees too: a woman writes désolée. You hear no difference, but you see it in a text message.

", "

Fixing the details

Once everyone agrees, you need a time and a place. The key verb is se retrouver (to meet up):

FrenchEnglish
On se retrouve à quelle heure ?What time shall we meet?
On se retrouve où ?Where shall we meet?
Rendez-vous devant la gare à sept heures.Let's meet in front of the station at seven.
On se retrouve chez moi ?Shall we meet at my place?
Je passe te prendre à huit heures.I'll pick you up at eight.
Je serai là vers midi.I'll be there around noon.

Un rendez-vous is any arranged meeting: with friends, with a doctor, or a date. It's not just romantic, unlike English \"rendezvous\".

Saying goodbye until then

À + the day or the time: À samedi !, À demain !, À ce soir !, À tout à l'heure ! (See you later today!)

A birthday invitation

Samedi, je fais une fête pour mes trente ans. Tu viendras ? Tu peux venir avec ta copine, bien sûr !On Saturday, I'm having a party for my thirtieth birthday. Will you come? You can bring your girlfriend, of course!
Volontiers ! J'apporterai le dessert. Je serai là vers vingt heures.I'd love to! I'll bring dessert. I'll be there around 8 p.m.

Even when you accept, a small offer is polite in France: J'apporte quelque chose ? (Shall I bring something?). The usual answer: Non, rien, juste toi !
